title: Joe Glaser, the Sunset and his kindness
summary: Glaser's mother owned the Sunset building; Hunter praises Glaser's big heart, the gangsters' generosity, and says she visited him every day until he died.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: It was in the '20s.
Yeah. I think --
The Sunset -- the building that housed the Sunset --
Yeah.
-- was either owned or managed -- I guess it was owned by Joe Glaser's mother.
It was? I didn't know that.
And Louis was at the Sunset. That's how Louis met Joe Glaser.
Uh-huh.
Because his mother was the landlord there.
I see. Uh-huh. He was crazy about his mother. Joe Glaser.
Yes. Yes.
Oh, he adored his mother. He was a wonderful man, Chris.
Was he? I wanted to ask you about that.

I want to tell you something about Joe Glaser. Joe Glaser might have been mixed up with gangsters and he might have been a gangster himself, but he was one of the finest gentlemen. If you were a lady, Joe Glaser treated you as a lady, and Joe --
End of tape 6
Joe Glaser had one of the biggest hearts in the world. Joe Glaser gave me $100.00 every year to send to my church. Every year. And always said, 'If you want more
you can have it." He was a wonderful, kind, tender hearted man, although he was very abrupt.
Uh-huh.
Very abrupt. But he adored Louis. He loved Louis. And he loved Miss Sarah Churchill, who was his secretary.
Uh-huh.
Sarah Churchill. He was a kind, good man. In fact, can I tell you something? All those gangsters were nice fellows.
Uh-huh.

May I tell you they all had hearts. In their way they might have been cruel, but they were all very kind to people. You know, they might have the ones that they wanted to get rid of or something like that, but they were big hearted and gentlemen.
But they killed their own.

They killed their own. They were gentlemen, kind hearted, and I bet you those gangsters have given up more money to charity than anybody else. Believe me when I tell you. Now, so now we finished about Joe Glaser.
Yes.
And I went to see him until he died. And the day he died I went to the hospital, but they wouldn't let me in. I went every day that he was sick, I went to the
hospital to see him, and I would go there and just stand and look at his lying in bed and walk away. He was unconscious. He didn't know it. But I would go just the same.
Uh-huh.
And the day he died I went right to that bed, and when they were getting ready to do him up to send him down to the morgue I was standing right there. He was a good man.
